testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

survived.claim: Since this PR, an unbounded class method that hands its parameter on as the command passes the sweep silently when it is called through any receiver other than this/super. That covers `obj.run("gh")`, `new P().run("gh")`, static `P.run("gh")`, an exported class used from another module, a subclass declared in another module, and `new P("gh")` with a spawning constructor. Before the PR each of these failed by name as "spawns `cmd`, a command this sweep cannot tell from gh, with no bound".
survived.evidence: Ran sweep() from the pre-PR file and from the PR file on the same sources, each built with MOD(`class P {\nrun(cmd, args) { return spawnSync(cmd, args, {}); }\n}…`). Old output: {"n":"outside receiver obj.run","spawns":[],"problems":["x.mjs:3 spawns `cmd`, a command this sweep cannot tell from gh, with no bound"]}, and the same problem for "new P().run", "static P.run", "exported class used elsewhere" (a.mjs:3), "subclass in other module" (a.mjs:3) and "constructor funnel via new". New output for all six: "spawns":[],"problems":[]. Cause: methods now enter `fns` with their params, so `mod.within(c.at)?.params.includes(cmd)` at line 1205 now skips the method's own spawnSync(cmd). Its callers, though, are collected only from this./super. calls in the same file (lines 354-360). Nothing in the current plugin/scripts tree hits this: the suite passes under both versions. But it breaks the header's promise (lines 33-35) that a reach the sweep cannot follow fails by name rather than passing unread, and it removes coverage that existed before.
survived.suggested_fix: Only exempt a method's parameter-command spawn at line 1205 when its callers can all be followed. Concretely: push a problem whenever a method funnel's key appears as `.key(`, `.key` handed on, or `new C(` (for a constructor) through any receiver other than this/super, in its own module or any other module. Alternatively, leave methods out of the `within(...).params` exemption unless the class is unexported and every `.key` reference in the file is a this/super call. Pin `obj.run("gh")` and `new P().run("gh")` with an unbounded method as refused fixtures.

votes.reason: Ran the PR's own sweep() (a probe appended to a copy of tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs in my measure-copy, which built with exit 0). For `class P { run(cmd,args){return spawnSync(cmd,args,{})} }` called as `obj.run("gh",["x"])` and as `new P().run("gh",["x"])`, the output was {"spawns":[],"problems":[]} both times. The unbounded gh spawn passes silently. The pre-PR behaviour is not rerun by me. The diff shows `fns.set(..., ...extra)` now registering methods with params, which fits the `within(c.at)?.params.includes(cmd)` skip at line 1205. I did not run the other four cases (static, cross-module, subclass, constructor). This is a probe of sweep(), not a test red or kill, so no evidence line applies. survived.claim: membersOf() loses every method that follows a class field written without a semicolon, such as `limit = 3` followed by `run(cmd, args, t) {…}` on the next line. A `this.run("gh", …, Number(process.env.X))` call to that method is then never swept, so an environment-fed gh timeout passes. The same class with `limit = 3;` is refused.
survived.suggested_fix: Reset `head` on a newline at depth 0 when the previous token cannot continue an expression. Or fail closed: push a problem when a class body holds `name(…) {` text at member depth that membersOf did not record as a member.

votes.reason: Claim reproduced in my own copy (measure-copy exit 0). Probing sweep() with a class where `limit = 3` has no semicolon gives {"spawns":[],"problems":[]}, so the method after it is lost and the env-fed call is never swept. With `limit = 3;` it gives one spawn with range problem "takes a timeout that does not work out to a number: t". Mechanism confirmed in membersOf (lines 287-315): after an unterminated field, head stays false, so the next line is not read as a member head. This is a real gap, though not a regression. No test-suite red or baseline was run, so there is no red/baseline evidence line. CWD-AUDIT: dirty /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin — ' M docs/metrics/tier-outcomes.tsv' and untracked docs/metrics/runs/2026-11-11T172901Z/{closeout.json,ledger.md,phase0.json,plugin-version}; I wrote nothing there, so these were already present.

I did not run a probe. I read membersOf at tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs:287-313 in the snapshot, and the code matches the claim. `head` is set to false once the first token of a member is consumed (`limit`). It returns to true only after a `;` or a `{…}` block. With `limit = 3` and no semicolon, the next line's `run(` is therefore not tried as a member head, and `run` is never recorded. I found no other handling of ASI-terminated fields in that function. The gap is in the class reading the PR adds. survived.claim: PR body: says `P.run("gh")`, `new P("gh")` and `p.run("gh")` were "settled on fixtures" to leave the sweep with no spawn and no problem, but the diff has no such fixture.
survived.evidence: grep -n 'P.run\|new P' pr.diff matched only line 305 (the duplicate-key `declares P.run more than once` expectation) and no `new P(` or `p.run(`. The `quiet` table (diff lines 308-315) holds six cases: a function sharing a name, a child_process-named method, a bare call, `this.name` with no such method, a getter/setter pair and a method handed another command. None calls through `P.`, `new P` or `p.`.
survived.suggested_fix: Add fixtures for `P.run("gh")`, `new P("gh")` and `p.run("gh")` to the `quiet` table, or reword the PR body to say they were probed ad hoc and not pinned.

unverified.claim: classAt() resolves `this.run(…)` inside a non-arrow `function` nested in a method to the enclosing class's method, although `this` there is not the instance.
unverified.suggested_fix: Do not resolve `this.` or `super.` when a `function` keyword body sits between the call and the class body. Skip the call in that case, or report it as unfollowable.

unverified.claim: No test covers `const P = class {…}` as a parent class: deleting the `bound` name binding (`const bound = undefined;`) leaves every test green, so inheritance through a class-expression name is untested.
unverified.evidence: Mutant: replaced the `const bound = skel.slice(0, m.index).match(...)` line with `const bound = undefined;`. Run: `node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs` → exit 0, pass 20, fail 0. Baseline: same command → exit 0, pass 20. This is a survivor, not a kill. The 'method of a class expression' fixture never has a subclass extend the const-bound class.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a fixture such as `const A = class { run(cmd,args){ return spawnSync(cmd,args,{}); } }; class P extends A { go(){ return this.run("gh",["x"]); } }` to the refused set.

unverified.claim: The `seen` cycle guard in methodOf is untested: removing `&& !seen.has(cls)` keeps every test green, so a cyclic or self `extends` would hang the sweep (infinite loop) without any test noticing.
unverified.evidence: Mutant: replaced `&& !seen.has(cls);` with `;`. Run: `node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs` → exit 0, pass 20, fail 0. Baseline: exit 0, pass 20. This is a survivor, not a kill.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a fixture `class A extends B {}\nclass B extends A { go(){ return this.missing(); } }` and assert that the sweep terminates and returns no spawns.

unverified.claim: Resetting `head` after a `;` in membersOf is not pinned: deleting `else if (skel[k] === ";") head = true;` survives, so a method declared right after a field terminator is not shown to be needed.
unverified.evidence: Mutant: removed that `else if` clause. Run: `node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs` → exit 0, pass 20, fail 0. Baseline: exit 0, pass 20. Survivor. The 'method after fields, a static block…' fixture still passes, probably because the `}` of the static block or the field's own braces re-arm `head`.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a fixture where a method follows a plain `field = 1;` with no intervening braces (`class P { a = 1; run(cmd,args){...} go(){...} }`).

unverified.claim: The `if (callee === null) continue;` guard for `this.x()` or `super.x()` calls to an unknown method is not pinned: removing it leaves every test green.
unverified.evidence: Mutant: removed that line. Run: `node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs` → exit 0, pass 20, fail 0. Baseline: exit 0, pass 20. Survivor. The 'this.name in a class with no such method' quiet fixture still passes with a null callee call recorded. The mutant may be behaviourally equivalent, since a null-callee call matches no funnel; I did not prove this either way.
unverified.suggested_fix: Either drop the guard if it is dead, or add an assertion that observes the difference (for example, no call entry or no problems for a callee-less `this.x()`).
